git.noProject: Open a project to follow the history of its files.
git.noBinary: Git is not installed on this computer. Version tracking needs it to work. Install it, then come back here.
git.uninitialised: This project does not follow its versions yet. Once tracking is set up, you record the state of your files whenever you like, and come back to it when you have to.
git.startHint: Prepares the project folder. Everything stays on this computer, nothing is sent anywhere.
git.refreshHint: Reads what has changed in the folder since the last look.
git.clean: Nothing has changed since the last recorded version.
git.messagePlaceholder: What you have just done, in one line
git.commitHint: Records the ticked files as a version you will be able to come back to.
git.restoreHint: Returns this file to the way the last recorded version has it.
git.stageAllHint: Adds every file of this group to the next version.
git.unstageAllHint: Takes every file of this group out of the next version.
git.branchHint: Shows the branches, and lets you move to another.
git.checkoutHint: Swings the folder over to this branch.
git.newBranchHint: Opens a variant from where you stand, losing nothing.
git.historyEmpty: No version recorded so far. The first one will appear here.
git.historyRefreshHint: Reads the list again from the top, to catch what was done outside the studio.
git.moreHint: Loads the rest of the history, underneath.
git.compareHint: Shows what changed in this file, down in the bottom band.
git.compareEmpty: Nothing to compare in this file.
git.compareUnavailable: This file cannot be compared. It may be too large, or missing from both versions.
git.compareNoBefore: This file did not exist yet.
git.fetchHint: Goes to see what the server has, changing nothing on your side.
git.pullHint: Brings home the versions recorded elsewhere.
git.pushHint: Puts your versions on the server, safe from whatever happens to this computer.
git.addRemoteHint: Ties this project to the server given, sending nothing yet.
git.tokenAsked: {{host}} refused access. Paste a personal token for that server: it is encrypted by the system keychain and never leaves this application.
git.tokenSaveHint: Encrypts the token on this computer, then runs the refused send again.
git.tokenHeld: A token is already held for {{host}}, and the server refused it. Paste another one, or forget this one.
git.tokenForgetHint: Erases the token held for this server. Nothing is sent, and the next send asks for one again.
git.keepOursHint: Keeps what you had, and drops what was arriving from the other side.
git.keepTheirsHint: Keeps what was arriving from the other side, and drops what you had.
git.abortMergeHint: Puts the folder back the way it was before the merge started.
git.stashHint: Puts your work in progress somewhere else, and gives it back when you want.
git.stashNowHint: Puts away everything that changed, new files included, leaving the folder clean.
git.stashPopHint: Puts this work back in the folder and takes it off the pile.
git.stashDropHint: Removes this pile without putting it back. Nothing retrieves it after that.
git.tagVersionHint: Gives it a name one can find again, rather than a run of characters.

failure.binaryMissing: Git cannot be found on this computer.
failure.notARepository: This folder does not follow its versions.
failure.locked: Another git command is busy in this folder. Wait for it to finish, then refresh.
failure.noIdentity: Git does not know what name to commit under. Fill it in from settings, under Versions.
failure.authentication: The remote server refused your credentials.
failure.network: The remote server cannot be reached.
failure.conflict: Some files are in conflict. Settle them before going on.
